svg.title: One duplicated key and the total is wrong
svg.desc: A whiteboard sketch showing a left table of three orders joined to a right table whose key A appears twice, ringed in red, so the result has four rows and the amount for A is counted twice, making a sum of 700 instead of 600 with no error; the fix of passing validate equals m colon 1 raising a MergeError instead; a bar chart of where a five-million-row DataFrame's 404.4 megabytes go, dominated by a 279.4 megabyte object column that becomes 5.0 megabytes as a category; and per-row costs of 112 nanoseconds for Series.apply against 0.4 nanoseconds vectorized, with iterrows at 9.33 microseconds per row struck through.
svg.text: One duplicated key and the total is wrong
one duplicated key on the RIGHT, and your revenue number is wrong
No error. No warning. Just wrong.
MergeError: Merge keys are not unique in right dataset
it fails AT THE JOIN instead of in the report
three days later. That is the whole value of the
object dtype is a column of POINTERS to Python
strings. That is where the 279 MB went - and why
251x between the top and the bottom
36x - and iterrows also destroys your dtypes
